title: Archer and Jeppesen ForeFlight unveil AI partnership
summary: Optimized for Apple silicon, the integration delivers real-time air traffic control transcription on iPad.
body_markdown:
[Archer Aviation](https://archer.com/) and[Jeppesen ForeFlight](https://www.jeppesenforeflight.com/) have announced the first phase of integrating Archer’s ZEE AI Foundation Model into[ForeFlight Mobile](https://foreflight.com/products/foreflight-mobile/) to enable real-time air traffic control (ATC) transcription in the leading electronic flight bag (EFB) for general aviation (GA) pilots.


Optimized for Apple silicon, the integration delivers real-time ATC transcription on iPad, helping pilots confirm clearances and catch errors before they become incidents.


Jeppesen ForeFlight is embarking on the first phase of integrating the real-time ATC transcription capabilities of[Archer’s purpose-built aviation foundation model, ZEE](https://archer.com/zee) , in ForeFlight Mobile to address a long-standing gap in the cockpit: ATC VHF communications still run over analog AM radio, so every instruction disappears the moment it is spoken.


ATC communication failures are a leading safety risk as they are a contributing factor in a majority of aviation incidents reported to NASA’s Aviation Safety Reporting System (ASRS), with readback errors exceeding 25% on transmissions carrying four or more instructions.


[ZEE’s AI Foundation Model integration into ForeFlight Mobile converts each radio call into readable text](https://archer.com/tech-blog/zee-decoding-the-airspace) in real time, giving pilots a reference they can revisit at any point in flight to confirm readbacks and catch errors potentially helping avoid incidents and improve safety.


The collaboration has already begun with Jeppesen ForeFlight evaluating the performance of Archer’s ZEE AI Foundation Model transcription capability on real radio communications, with the goal of giving pilots a dependable aid that supports their own judgment and their communication with ATC.


Developed by Archer’s in-house AI team, ZEE is the industry’s first foundation model capable of running on-device with no connectivity while delivering high accuracy transcription pilots need in real aviation operations.


ZEE’s ability to transcribe instructions as soon as they’re spoken is enabled by the model’s training on over 100,000 hours of real-world ATC radio communications.


“Today is an important step forward for pilot safety,” said Adam Goldstein, founder and CEO of Archer.


“Every pilot knows the moment when you read back a clearance and wonder whether you heard it right. Air traffic control still runs on analog radio, and an instruction is gone the second it’s spoken. We built ZEE to change that. Putting it in ForeFlight Mobile gives pilots a written record of every instruction, in the cockpit, in the app they already trust.”


“Accuracy, safety and trust guide everything we build for pilots, and they guide this integration too. We’re evaluating how Archer’s ZEE AI Foundation Model can bring real-time ATC transcription to ForeFlight Mobile and help pilots verify readbacks and catch errors,” said Travis Root, senior vice president – Product and Engineering, Flight Deck, Jeppesen ForeFlight.


“As a pilot, I know a misheard clearance is a stressful moment in flight,” said Mario Srouji, vice president, AI Products, at Archer. “Partnering with Jeppesen ForeFlight to integrate the transcription capability of our ZEE Foundation Model in ForeFlight Mobile is a first step toward giving pilots a clear, accurate record of what ATC said.”


*This press release was prepared and distributed by Archer Aviation.*
